n395cdcc96e3.s: Which power first replaced the Indo-Greeks in the north-west?
n395cdcc96e3.x: The Sakas replaced the Indo-Greeks first; they were followed by the Parthians (Pahlavas) and then the Kushanas.

nf96137b9f33.s:
Consider the following statements about the foreign groups in ancient India:
1. The Indo-Greeks appeared before the Sakas.
2. The Parthians appeared before the Sakas.
3. The Kushanas appeared after the Parthians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nf96137b9f33.x: The order was Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Parthians and Kushanas, so statement 2 is wrong: the Parthians came after the Sakas.

nf94c50e7cf3.s: The Kshaharata branch of the Western Kshatrapas ruled in:
nf94c50e7cf3.x: The Kshaharatas held the Western Deccan, while the Kardamakas ruled around Ujjain, Malwa and Kathiawar.

nindian-history-9-2.s: To convert a Saka year into the AD year, one must add:
nindian-history-9-2.x: The AD year is the Saka year plus 78 (not 77), since the Saka era began in 78 AD.

n468de3951c5.s: The Second Buddhist Council was held at:
n468de3951c5.x: The Second Council met at Vaishali; the First was at Rajagriha, the Third at Pataliputra and the Fourth in Kashmir.

new.s: The largest ancient gold coin, of 20 staters, was issued by the Indo-Greek ruler:
new.x: Eucratides issued the largest ancient gold coin, weighing 20 staters.

new.s: The last Indo-Greek ruler, whose defeat ended Greek rule south of the Hindu Kush, was:
new.x: Hermaius was the last Indo-Greek ruler; Demetrius was the first and Menander the greatest.

new.s: The Indo-Greek ruler Strato was the son of:
new.x: Strato was Menander's son.

new.s: The capital of the Indo-Greek king Menander was:
new.x: Menander ruled from Sakala (Sialkot), not Taxila.

new.s: The Milindapanho was written in which language?
new.x: The Milindapanho, the 'Questions of Milinda', is a Pali text, not a Sanskrit one.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Menander?
o: His coins carry the Buddhist wheel
new.x: Heliodorus was sent to Vidisha by Antialcidas, not by Menander.

new.s: The Romaka Siddhanta reflects Greek influence on Indian:
new.x: Greek influence in astronomy is seen in the Romaka Siddhanta and the term Hora (horoscope).

new.s: Heliodorus came as envoy of Antialcidas to the court of the Sunga king:
new.x: Heliodorus of Taxila was sent by Antialcidas to the Sunga king Bhagabhadra at Vidisha.

new.s: The Besnagar Garuda pillar of Heliodorus honours:
new.x: Heliodorus, who called himself a Bhagavata, set up the Besnagar Garuda pillar in honour of Vasudeva.

new.s: Gedrosia, a region of the ancient north-west, corresponds to today's:
new.x: Gedrosia is today's Balochistan and is not linked to the Indo-Greeks; Scythia was the land of the Sakas.

new.s: The silver coin Rupaka was issued after defeating the Sakas by:
new.x: Chandragupta II issued the silver Rupaka after his victory over the Sakas.

new.s: Coins bearing the figure of Lakshmi, some with the Arabic Kalma, were issued by:
new.x: Muhammad Ghori issued coins with Lakshmi, some with the Arabic Kalma; it was not Chandragupta II.

new.s: The Taxila copper plate is associated with:
new.x: The Taxila copper plate belongs to Patika, not Menander.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Indo-Greek coinage:
1. Most Indo-Greek coins were of silver and copper.
2. More than 30 Indo-Greek kings are known mainly from their coins.
3. The Kushanas issued gold coins in India before the Indo-Greeks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Indo-Greek coins were mostly silver and copper and reveal 30+ kings; statement 3 is wrong because the Indo-Greeks issued the first gold coins and the Kushanas only made gold large-scale.

new.s: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is associated with the Parthian ruler:
new.x: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription belongs to Gondophares, the greatest Parthian ruler, not to a Saka ruler.

new.s: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription of Gondophares was found near:
new.x: Takht-i-Bahi lies near Peshawar.

new.s: The gift of a village to the monks of the Karle chaitya was made by:
new.x: The Karle inscription records Ushavadatta's gift of a village to the monks; Junnar belongs to Ayama.

new.s: Ushavadatta deposited money with the Govardhana weavers' guild at an annual interest of:
new.x: The Nasik record says 2,000 karshapanas were deposited with the weavers' guild at 12% a year.

new.s: Ayama, who issued the Junnar (Manmodi) cave inscription, was Nahapana's:
new.x: Ayama was Nahapana's minister (amatya); Ushavadatta was his son-in-law.

new.s: Under Rudradaman I, Sudarshana lake was repaired by his Pahlava minister:
new.x: Suvishakha repaired the lake for Rudradaman I; Pushyagupta built it, Tushaspha added canals and Chakrapalita repaired it later.

new.s: Canals were added to Sudarshana lake during Ashoka's reign by:
new.x: The Yavanaraja Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka.

new.s: Chakrapalita repaired Sudarshana lake in the reign of:
new.x: Chakrapalita, son of governor Parnadatta, repaired the lake in the Gupta period under Skandagupta.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I?
o: It records victories over Satakarni and the Yaudheyas
It is the first long inscription in Prakrit
It records the repair of Sudarshana lake
new.x: It is the first long inscription in Sanskrit; earlier long records were in Prakrit.

new.s: Patika, known from the Taxila copper plate, belonged to the Shaka branch centred at:
new.x: Liaka Kusulaka and Patika ruled the north-western Shaka branch at Taxila.

new.s: Rajuvula and Sodasa ruled the Shaka branch centred at:
new.x: Rajuvula and Sodasa were Shaka rulers of Mathura.

new.s: Bhumaka and Nahapana belonged to which Shaka branch?
new.x: Bhumaka and Nahapana were Kshaharatas of Nasik; Chashtana and Rudradaman I were Kardamakas.

new.s: Rudradaman I ruled c. 130-150 CE from:
new.x: Rudradaman I, a Kardamaka, ruled from Ujjain.

new.s: The Kali era began in:
new.x: The Kali era traditionally begins in 3102 BC; 57 BC is Vikrama, 78 AD Saka and 248 AD Kalachuri.

new.s: The Harsha era, marking Harshavardhana's accession, began in:
new.x: The Harsha era began in 606 AD; 319 AD is Gupta, 248 AD Kalachuri and 1119 AD Lakshmana Sena.

new.s: In a leap year, 1 Chaitra of the national calendar falls on:
new.x: 1 Chaitra is 22 March in a normal year and 21 March in a leap year.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Shakas and Kushanas:
1. They introduced trousers, long coats, helmets and boots.
2. Their military strength lay mainly in elephants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: They introduced trousers, long coats, helmets and boots; their military edge was better cavalry, not elephants.

new.s: The vice-president of the Fourth Buddhist Council was:
new.x: Ashvaghosha was vice-president; Vasumitra presided over the Council.

new.s: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held at:
new.x: The Fourth Council met at Kundalvana (Harwan) in Kashmir under Kanishka, not at Pataliputra.

new.s: The proceedings of the Fourth Buddhist Council were in:
new.x: The Fourth Council was the first in Sanskrit; earlier councils used Pali or Prakrit.

new.s: The Rabatak inscription of Kanishka is written in:
new.x: The Rabatak inscription is in the Bactrian language written in Greek script.

new.s: The Sarnath Bodhisattva image of year 3 of Kanishka was dedicated by:
new.x: Friar Bala dedicated the Sarnath Bodhisattva image in year 3 of Kanishka (81 AD).

new.s: The Rabatak inscription was discovered in Afghanistan in:
new.x: The Rabatak inscription was found in 1993 near Surkh Kotal, Afghanistan.

new.s: The Kushana army that marched against Pan Chao in 86 AD numbered about:
new.x: About 70,000 Kushana troops marched against Pan Chao in 86 AD and lost to a smaller Chinese force.

new.s: Kanishka's title 'Kaisara' reflects influence from:
new.x: Kaisara (Caesar) came from Rome; Devaputra from China, Shaonano Shao from Persia and Maharaja from India.

new.s: Vima Kadphises, who took the title Sarvaloka Ishvara, was the father of:
new.x: Vima Kadphises was the father of Kanishka.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Six-headed Kartikeya on coins – Vima Kadphises
new.x: Six-headed Kartikeya with a peacock appears on Yaudheya copper coins, not on those of Vima Kadphises.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about early Buddha images:
1. The Gandhara school shows a standing Buddha in pleated robes.
2. The Mathura school shows a seated Buddha with a halo.
3. The Amaravati school used red sandstone for its narrative panels.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Gandhara shows a standing Buddha and Mathura a seated one with a halo; Amaravati panels are of white limestone, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: The Kushanas belonged to which people?
new.x: The Kushanas were Yueh-chi (Yuezhi) from north-west China and Central Asia.

new.s: The Manusmriti described Shakas and Kushans who did not follow priestly customs as:
new.x: The Manusmriti called Shakas, Kushans, Hunas and Pratiharas who did not follow priestly customs 'Fallen Kshatriyas'.

new.s: Which scholar of Kanishka's court urged the holding of the Fourth Buddhist Council?
new.x: Parshva, a Buddhist scholar, urged Kanishka to hold the Council.
